_RELIC_NAME: 유물 128종 이름 (1017 · 유물의 법칙 1단계 — RELIC_DB) — 전역 키: 세이브 · 서버에 남는 유물 이름을 런타임(toCur · toKo)이 이 표로 바꾼다. 다른 글과 겹치지 않게
_RELIC_LORE: 유물 사연 · 양날 까닭 · 공명 (직업 유물이 그 직업 학생에게 끼면)
No one knows who set it spinning, yet it still turns in a corner of the practice grounds. Run with it in hand and you won't get winded as fast.
멈추지 못하니 막을 틈도 없다: It can't stop, so there's no moment to block
연습장 옆 도랑에 띄운 종이배는 꼭 돌아온다. 그래서 원정 가는 날이면: A paper boat set afloat in the ditch beside the practice grounds always comes back. So on expedition days, everyone folds one and tucks it away.
종이라 젖으면 흐물흐물해진다: It's paper — it goes limp when wet
시험 답을 적었다가 급히 지운 밀랍판. 지운 글씨일수록 더 또렷이 남는다: A wax tablet where someone wrote exam answers, then hastily wiped them away. The more you erase, the clearer it lingers. Since you can just wipe it and write again, no one at the practice grounds buys paper anymore.
지운 답을 떠올리느라 겨눔이 흐려진다: Recalling erased answers blurs your aim
한 짝뿐인 빨간 구두. 주인을 찾아다니는지 어느 원정지에서든 불쑥 나온다: A single red shoe. Perhaps it's searching for its owner — it turns up at every expedition site.
한 짝뿐이라 걸음이 엇나간다: With only one shoe, your steps go askew
친구끼리 나눠 매는 매듭. 한 번 묶으면 칼로 끊기 전에는 풀리지 않는다: A knot friends tie together. Once tied, they say it won't come undone unless cut by a blade.
A button fallen from a uniform. On days you pick it up, things go strangely well.
운을 믿으면 덜 겨눈다: Trust luck, and you aim less
어느 졸업생의 허리띠에서 떨어진 버클. 소용돌이 무늬가 닳아 반들반들하다: A buckle fallen from some graduate's belt. Its swirl pattern is worn smooth and shiny.
꽉 조인 허리는 굼뜨다: A tightly cinched waist moves sluggishly
A letter whose seal was never broken. The mist has erased the recipient's name. Keep it close, and you remember where you belong.
돌아갈 곳이 떠오르면 칼끝이 무뎌진다: Thinking of home dulls the blade's edge
무너진 성의 깃발 조각. 문장은 닳아 없어졌지만, 든 사람이 새 이름을: A scrap of a fallen castle's banner. Its crest has worn away, but it flutters until its bearer earns a new name.
깃발을 든 사람은 눈에 띈다: Whoever carries a banner stands out
The outstretched hand of a statue in the ruins' garden. It never let go of the green stone in its palm.
열쇠를 잃은 성의 자물쇠. 잠긴 채로 무엇을 지키는지 이제 아무도 모른다: A castle lock whose key was lost. It stays locked, though no one remembers what it guards.
The castle queen's hand mirror. The true heart of whoever looks into it rises up like starlight.
옛 성의 공주가 쓰던 빗. 이걸로 머리를 빗은 날엔 말에 힘이 실린다고: A comb once used by the old castle's princess. They say on days you comb your hair with it, your words carry weight.
안개 속에서도 꺼지지 않는 등불. 들고 있는 동안은 지쳐도 한 걸음 더: A lantern that won't go out even in the mist. While you hold it, you can take one more step even when exhausted.
등불을 든 사람은 어둠 속에서 가장 먼저 보인다: In the dark, whoever holds the lantern is seen first
본선 우승 학원에 건네는 옛 왕관. 금은 갈라졌어도, 쓴 사람이 이기면: An old crown handed to the academy that wins the Finals. Its gold is cracked, but when its wearer wins, people remember that name for a long time.
A chain from the old castle's dungeon. Once one link opened, it never closed again. It makes past sins weigh a little lighter, too.
성문에 매달려 있던 문고리. 짐승의 얼굴은 두드리는 사람을 끝까지 내려다: A knocker that once hung on the castle gate. Its beast face glares down at whoever knocks, to the very end.
종탑 창틀에 앉아 있던 도자기 부엉이. 밤새 별을 세던 눈이라 공부하는: A ceramic owl that sat on the bell tower's windowsill. Its eyes counted stars all night, so it's good company for a studying student.
밤을 새우면 낮에 힘이 빠진다: Stay up all night, and you're drained by day
종탑 꼭대기에서 잡은 구름. 마개를 열면 이슬비가 조금 내린다. 훈련장에: A cloud caught atop the bell tower. Uncork it and a little drizzle falls. Leave it open at the training grounds and sweat cools in no time.
구름처럼 가볍게 친다: It strikes as lightly as a cloud
A butterfly that flew out of the bell tower's stained glass. As light as it is, it breaks just as easily.
가벼운 만큼 잘 깨진다: As light as it is, it breaks just as easily
태엽을 감으면 종탑의 종소리를 흉내 낸다. 마지막 한 음은 늘 반 박자: Wind it up and it mimics the bell tower's chimes. The last note always comes half a beat early.
그늘에서만 시간을 가리키는 해시계. 바늘은 종탑이 무너진 시각에 멈춰 있: A sundial that tells time only in the shade. Its needle is stopped at the hour the bell tower fell.
흔들면 무너지기 전의 종탑 위로 눈이 내린다. 들여다보고 있으면 마음이: Shake it, and snow falls over the bell tower as it stood before it fell. Gazing into it calms the heart.
마음이 가라앉으면 칼끝도 가라앉는다: When the heart settles, so does the blade
A star the bell tower's astronomer caught and kept. The cage door opens only from the inside.
종탑을 무너뜨린 게 이 돌이라는 말이 있다. 아직도 속이 달아 있고, 쥔: Some say this is the stone that brought down the bell tower. Its core is still hot, and it weighs heavy in the hand.
쥔 손이 무겁다: It weighs heavy in the hand
누군가 종탑 꼭대기에서 달을 병에 담았다. 그날부터 탑 위의 달은 반쪽이: Someone bottled the moon atop the bell tower. Ever since, the moon above the tower has been only half.
광역 대회 우승기 끝에 박혀 있던 수정 눈. 감기지 않는 눈은 상대가 숨: A crystal eye once set at the tip of the Regional Tournament's victory banner. An eye that never closes sees even what an opponent hides.
소금 바다의 소금 한 줌. 문턱에 뿌리면 나쁜 것이 따라 들어오지 못한다: A handful of salt from the Salt Sea. Scatter it on the threshold and nothing evil can follow you in.
짠 것을 품으면 목이 말라 걸음이 무겁다: Carry salt and thirst makes your steps heavy
A small anchor from who knows what ship. Hold it, and your heart won't drift away.
닻은 붙잡아 두는 물건이다: An anchor is made to hold you in place
When the moon rises, the shell opens on its own. The pearl inside is cold to the touch.
A cup carved by the sea. Pour water in and the salty taste vanishes.
The helm of a ship swallowed by the rift. Lay a hand on it and it turns by itself toward where you must go.
소금 바다가 아직 바다였을 때의 생물. 나선을 따라가다 보면 처음 배운: A creature from when the Salt Sea was still a sea. Follow its spiral and you return to the first things you learned.
The canteen of a pilgrim who crossed the Salt Sea. No matter how much you drink, you never see the bottom.
Each time you unfold it, the road grows by one more square. No one has unfolded it all the way yet.
이계의 균열, 맨 밑바닥에서만 자라는 검은 진주. 들여다보면 깊이를 모를: A black pearl that grows only at the very bottom of the Otherworld's rift. Look into it, and a darkness of unknowable depth stares back.
Fare money buried with the dead. The sun face stamped on it belongs to no known kingdom.
죽은 이의 노잣돈은 산 사람의 기운을 조금 가져간다: The dead's fare money takes a little of the living's vigor
천 년 전에 갇힌 작은 벌레가 아직도 손님처럼 앉아 있다. 쥐고 있으면: A tiny insect trapped a thousand years ago still sits inside like a guest. Hold it, and wounds open more slowly.
무덤에 바친 돌 석류. 알알이 박힌 석류석은 지금도 조금씩 붉게 익어 간: A stone pomegranate offered at the tomb. The garnets studding it still ripen a little redder, bit by bit.
An urn sealed with red wax. Shake it, and someone inside answers.
무덤 주인의 가슴에 얹혀 있던 풍뎅이. 쓰러져도 다시 일어나라는 뜻이었다: A scarab laid on the chest of the tomb's master. They say it meant: even if you fall, rise again.
Five cracks, each filled with gold. What has broken and mended knows how to break again.
깨졌다 붙은 것은 다시 깨질 줄도 안다: What has broken and mended knows how to break again
An egg kept warm in the innermost chamber of the tomb. Through its crack, a blue light breathes.
죽은 이의 마음을 달던 저울. 한쪽으로 기운 채 다시는 바로 서지 않지만: Scales that once weighed the hearts of the dead. They lean to one side and never stand straight again, but they weigh the price of goods precisely.
기운 채 다시는 바로 서지 않는다: Once tilted, they never stand straight again
A piece of the sun disk that lay atop a coffin in the Otherworld tomb — the sun of that other sky. It stays lukewarm even after sundown.
이계 무덤의 가장 깊은 방, 관 대신 놓여 있던 상자. 이음매의 빛은 쥔: A box that lay where a coffin should have been, in the deepest chamber of the Otherworld tomb. The light in its seams pulses with its holder's heartbeat — and wears them out just as much.
Honey that never spoils. It's been handed down, jar and all, since the Old Farmer's grandfather's day.
단 것을 먹으면 늘어진다: Eat sweets, and you get sluggish
할아버지네 참나무에 딱 한 번 열린 도토리. 다람쥐도 이건 건드리지 않았: An acorn that grew just once on the old farmer's oak. Even the squirrels left it alone.
가을마다 할아버지가 채워 주는 바구니. 고운 돌 셋은 빈 바구니가 서운하: A basket the old farmer fills every autumn. The three pretty stones are there so it won't feel lonely when empty.
먹을 수 없는 사과. 그래도 바라보고 있으면 배가 부르다고 할아버지는 말: An apple you can't eat. Still, the old farmer says just looking at it fills you up.
밭 가장자리에 두면 사흘 안에 비가 온다. 동전 위에 앉은 건 덤이라는데: Set it at the edge of a field and rain comes within three days. The coin it sits on is a bonus, they say — and its owner's wages get a bonus too.
A bone the hunter saves every evening. It waits for someone to split it in two.
반으로 갈라지려고 남겨 둔 뼈다: It's a bone kept to be snapped in half
A copper whistle once used to call hounds. Blow it, and faraway things turn to look this way.
부르면 적도 돌아본다: Call out, and enemies turn too
숲 깊은 곳에서 캐 온 버섯. 사냥꾼은 먹으면 안 된다고 몇 번이나 말했: A mushroom dug up deep in the forest. The hunter warned, again and again, never to eat it.
먹으면 안 된다고 했다 — 독이 있다: You were told not to eat it — it's poisonous
The Innkeeper's treasured teacup. Even empty, it feels warm in the hand.
바늘에 찔리지 않게 끼는 은 골무. 원장은 이것 하나로 삼십 년을 버텼다: A silver thimble worn to keep needles from pricking. The Salon Owner says it alone saw them through thirty years.
골무를 끼면 손끝이 둔하다: With a thimble on, your fingertips go dull
실을 감을수록 무거워지는 물레추. 다 감으면 이야기 하나가 끝난다고 한다: A spindle that grows heavier the more thread you wind. They say when it's full, a story comes to an end.
감을수록 무거워진다: The more you wind, the heavier it gets
시내 대회 우승 상품으로 내려오는 상아 주사위. 던진 사람이 바라는 눈보: Ivory dice passed down as the City Tournament's champion prize. They always roll one higher than the thrower hoped.
The tile always laid down last at the tavern. Whoever holds it ends the game.
판을 끝낼 때까지 손에서 내려놓지 못한다: You can't put it down until the game is over
먼 나라 상인이 술값 대신 두고 간 부채. 부치면 바람이 엉뚱한 쪽에서: A fan a merchant from a faraway land left instead of paying for drinks. Wave it, and the wind blows from the wrong direction. Flash it open, and merchants lower their prices first.
바람이 엉뚱한 쪽에서 분다: The wind blows from the wrong direction
안에 인형이 몇 개 들었는지는 열어 본 사람마다 말이 다르다. 하나를 찾: Everyone who opens it gives a different count of the dolls inside. Find one, and another turns up.
속삭임에 귀를 기울이다 겨눔을 놓친다: Listening to the whispers, you lose your aim
A candle the Sister lit for night prayers. It never burned down — only the blue flame remains.
촛불은 바람 한 번에 흔들린다: A candle flame wavers at a single breath of wind
목수의 화덕에서 쓰던 풀무. 한 번 눌러 주면 꺼져 가던 불씨가 살아난다: Bellows from the Carpenter's hearth. One squeeze, and a dying ember flares back to life.
불을 키우다 보면 막을 생각을 잊는다: Stoking the fire, you forget to guard
도구상 진열대 구석에서 굴러온 구슬. 보는 쪽마다 다른 색이 위로 올라온: A marble that rolled out from a corner of the Tool Merchant's shelf. A different color rises to the top from every angle — and it shares out its powers evenly, too.
선배가 두고 간 호박빛 안경. 쓰면 칠판 글씨가 유난히 또렷해진다 — 그: Amber-tinted glasses a senior left behind. Put them on and the writing on the board looks unusually sharp — that senior was always top of the class, they say.
앞만 또렷하고 옆은 흐리다: Sharp straight ahead, blurry to the sides
신입생들이 부적처럼 지니고 다니던 도자기 곰. 깨질 때마다 누군가 금으로: A porcelain bear new students carried like a charm. Every time it broke, someone mended it with gold.
학원 표본실 선반에서 떨어진 고사리 화석. 잎맥을 따라 흐르는 금빛처럼,: A fern fossil that fell from a shelf in the academy's specimen room. Like the gold flowing along its veins, old things know how to teach.
왕가의 마지막 찻자리에 올랐던 주전자. 금으로 메운 금이 깨지기 전보다: A teapot served at the royal family's last tea. Its gold-filled cracks are stronger than it was before it broke.
여왕이 마상 시합의 기사에게 건넸다는 레이스 손수건. 루비 핀은 아직도: A lace handkerchief the queen is said to have given a knight at a joust. Its ruby pin is still cold.
A hexagonal lacquer box with its lid slightly ajar. Only the box knows what it once held.
옛 왕궁 알현실 바닥의 한 조각. 해 무늬 한가운데를 밟을 수 있는 사람: A piece of the old palace's throne room floor. Only the king was allowed to step on the center of the sun pattern.
태엽을 감으면 은 백조가 한 바퀴 돈다. 종탑이 무너진 뒤로는 늘 같은: Wind it up and a silver swan makes one turn. Since the bell tower fell, it always stops at the same bar.
넋 놓고 듣다 보면 경계를 놓친다: Listen in a daze and you drop your guard
A copper funnel from the bell tower's observatory. Pour the night sky through it and only bits of stars are left behind.
종탑 꼭대기에서 노을을 받아 금빛이 된 깃털. 깃대 끝은 펜촉처럼 깎여: A feather turned gold by the sunset atop the bell tower. Its quill is cut like a pen nib.
종탑 꼭대기에서 달빛을 떠 마셨다는 은 숟가락. 오목한 자리에 초승달이: A silver spoon said to have scooped up and sipped moonlight atop the bell tower. A crescent moon is engraved in its bowl.
균열의 차가운 물에서 헤엄치던 그대로 얼어 버린 물고기. 손바닥 위에서도: A fish frozen mid-swim in the rift's cold waters. It won't melt even in your palm.
얼음을 쥔 손은 곱는다: Hands that hold ice go numb
바다 밑에서 진주가 포도송이처럼 맺혔다. 한 알을 떼어 내면 다음 날 그: Pearls that formed like a bunch of grapes on the seabed. Pluck one, and another forms in its place the next day.
사막을 건너온 순례자의 짐에서 나온 향수병. 몸을 정결히 하던 향이라,: A perfume bottle from the pack of a pilgrim who crossed the desert. It was a scent for purifying the body, so when you uncork it, the smell of sandstorms comes first.
균열 바닥의 조약돌 위에 자란 장밋빛 산호. 귀에 대면 바다가 처음 갈라: Rose-colored coral that grew on a pebble at the bottom of the rift. Hold it to your ear and you hear the day the sea first split open.
용사의 관 곁에서 천 년을 버틴 돌거북. 등딱지의 모자이크가 아직 반들거: A stone tortoise that endured a thousand years beside the hero's coffin. The mosaic on its shell still gleams.
무덤 제단에 새겨진 연꽃이 떨어져 나온 것. 돌인데도 꽃잎 안쪽이 따뜻하: A lotus carved on the tomb's altar that broke away. Though it's stone, the inside of its petals is warm.
용사의 말이 신던 말굽. 어디에 두고 와도 다음 날 아침이면 마구간 앞에: A horseshoe worn by the hero's steed. They say no matter where it was left, the next morning it would be lying in front of the stable.
부장품 사이에서 나온 황금 호두. 갈라진 틈으로 보랏빛 결정이 보이지만,: A golden walnut found among the grave goods. Purple crystals show through the crack, but no one has managed to open it.
접힌 채로 비를 기다리는 양산. 펴 본 사람은 없는데, 원정지 어디서든: A folded parasol waiting for rain. No one has ever opened it, yet it turns up in someone's pack at every expedition site.
양산을 든 손은 칼을 쥐지 못한다: A hand holding a parasol can't hold a sword
에메랄드 껍데기를 진 금 달팽이. 느리지만 어디에든 먼저 와 있다 — 누: A golden snail carrying an emerald shell. Slow, yet it's always there first — in anyone's pocket.
느리다 — 그래도 먼저 와 있다: Slow — but it still gets there first
꼭지가 하나로 이어진 루비 앵두 한 쌍. 둘이 함께 다니면 운도 두 배라: A pair of ruby cherries joined at a single stem. They say when two go together, their luck doubles.
여관 안주인이 겨울밤 손님 잠자리를 데우던 화로. 뚜껑 구멍마다 아직 숯: The brazier the Innkeeper used to warm guests' beds on winter nights. Every hole in its lid still smells of charcoal.
여관 안주인이 원정 가는 학생들 짐에 넣어 주던 주전자. 찌그러진 자리마: The kettle the Innkeeper tucked into the packs of students heading off on expeditions. Every dent holds a story from the road.
미용실 원장이 아끼던 은 가위. 머리카락과 함께 묵은 인연도 잘라 준다고: The Salon Owner's treasured silver shears. They say they cut away stale ties along with your hair.
자르는 것은 나도 벤다: What cuts can cut you too
목수가 아이들 주려고 깎은 흔들 목마. 타고 흔들다 잠들면 꿈속에서도 달: A rocking horse the Carpenter carved for the children. Fall asleep rocking on it, and you keep galloping in your dreams.
목수가 옛 성문에서 떼어 온 나비 경첩. 안과 밖의 경계를 지키던 쇠라: A butterfly hinge the Carpenter pried off an old castle gate. Iron that once guarded the line between inside and out, it still won't turn easily.
도구상 계산대를 지키던 셈판. 알을 튕기면 값이 맞는지 틀린지 소리가 다: The abacus that guarded the Tool Merchant's counter. Flick its beads and the sound tells you whether a price is right or wrong.
수녀님이 샘물을 길어 오던 주전자. 금으로 메운 주둥이에서 물이 끊긴 적: The pitcher the Sister used to draw spring water. Water has never stopped flowing from its gold-mended spout.
세례 때 수녀님이 아기 손에 쥐여 주던 은 딸랑이. 흔들면 첫 울음처럼: A silver rattle the Sister placed in babies' hands at baptism. Shake it and it rings out clear, like a first cry.
사냥꾼이 한겨울 숲에서 주워 온 얼음 솔방울. 봄이 와도 녹지 않고 쥔: An ice pinecone the hunter picked up in the forest in deep winter. Even when spring comes, it doesn't melt, and it chills the hand that holds it.
쥔 손이 시리다: The hand that holds it goes cold
밭 할아버지가 손녀 주려고 아껴 두던 유리 딸기. 설탕을 입힌 것처럼 반: A glass strawberry the old farmer was saving for his granddaughter. It sparkles as if coated in sugar.
유리라 쉽게 깨진다: It's glass, so it breaks easily
용사의 무덤을 지키던 기사단장의 반지. 방패 모양 사파이어 안에 맹세한: The ring of the knight commander who guarded the Hero's Tomb. Inside its shield-shaped sapphire, the names of everyone who swore the oath are engraved one over another.
A reliquary said to hold the light of dawn. Even with the lid closed, light leaks through the gaps.
백 번 찍혀도 쓰러지지 않았다는 기사의 문장. 칼자국마다 리벳을 박아 다: The crest of a knight said never to have fallen, even after a hundred blows. Every sword gash was riveted and the crest set upright again.
싸움에서 돌아올 때마다 한 번씩 고쳐 묶은 검매듭. 매듭의 수가 곧 살아: A sword knot retied once each time its owner came home from battle. The number of knots is the number of days they returned alive.
The broken tip of a magic sword. When another blade comes near, it rings in the same tone.
마검이 저절로 뽑히지 않게 채워 두던 고리. 풀어 주면 칼이 먼저 앞으로: A ring fastened to keep a magic sword from drawing itself. Loosen it, and the blade leaps forward first.
성터 예배당에서 나온 은 성배. 마신 만큼 채워 주지만, 먼저 조금 가져: A silver chalice from the chapel in the ruins. It gives back as much as you drink — but takes a little first.
마신 만큼 채워 주지만 먼저 조금 가져간다: It gives back as much as you drink, but takes a little first
A forbidden book bound in chains. No one opens it, yet each night another page has turned.
A key that fits no door in the ruins. Insert it into a shadow, and it turns.
A vial with a serpent coiled around it. Every time you uncork it, the serpent coils once more.
A fox mask that hides your face only within the moon's shadow. On full-moon nights, its expression changes.
A scroll that unrolls without a sound. Only those who read the techniques written on it remember them.
An hourglass whose sand falls upward. It has run backward since the day the bell tower fell.
북쪽 대신 '아까'를 가리키는 나침반. 바늘을 따라가면 지나간 순간에 닿: A compass that points to ‘a moment ago’ instead of north. Follow the needle and you reach a moment already past.
무너진 종탑의 가장 작은 종. 큰 종들이 떨어질 때 혼자 울리지 않고 남: The smallest bell of the fallen bell tower. When the great bells fell, it alone stayed behind, silent.
A censer that never went out in the bell tower's chapel. Its smoke always drifts toward the wounded.
종소리를 한 번 더 들려주는 하프 브로치. 노래를 멈춰도 마지막 음이 남: A harp brooch that lets you hear the bell's toll once more. Even when the song stops, the last note lingers.
종탑의 바람이 불어 주던 피리. 관 하나는 아직 아무도 소리를 내 본 적: Pipes once played by the bell tower's wind. One of the tubes has never been sounded by anyone.
A crystal formed from magic that seeped out of the rift. Shine light into it and it comes out as a spell.
물 · 불 · 바람이 한 구슬 안에서 서로를 쫓는다. 셋이 만나는 순간: Water, fire, and wind chase each other inside a single orb. The moment all three meet, the spell is complete.
Thread twisted from mana. However much is wound, that much of a foe's power it can bind.
A hexagonal sealstone dredged from the bottom of the rift. The runes carved into it pass onto weapons.
A core holding the rift's pulse. Clench it in your fist and your hand moves first.
A red catalyst that gathers mana into one place. The more you use it, the hotter the seal on the back of your hand burns.
선배 무도가가 연습장 기둥에 걸어 두고 간 염주. 알을 굴릴 때마다 숨이: Prayer beads a senior monk hung on a pillar at the practice grounds. Each bead you roll deepens your breath.
연습장 구석 상자에 남아 있던 붕대. 감으면 아픈 줄 모르고 한 판 더: Bandages left in a box in a corner of the practice grounds. Wrap them on and you forget the pain and stand up for one more round.
사격 연습장 과녁 밑에서 나온 탄실. 여섯 칸 중 한 칸에는 늘 행운이: A revolver cylinder found under a target at the shooting range. One of its six chambers always holds luck.
A scope left behind by a gunner who graduated. Look through it and the target comes to you first.
A feather left by the hunter's beloved hawk. Tuck it beside your bowstring and you can see the wind.
사냥꾼이 젊을 때 차던 가죽 팔찌. 시위를 놓는 순간 바람이 한 번 더: A leather bracer the hunter wore in their youth. The instant you release the string, the wind gives one more push.
할아버지네 밭에서 백 년째 싹을 틔우지 않는 씨앗. 숲지기의 손에서만 따: A seed that hasn't sprouted in a hundred years in the old farmer's field. It grows warm only in a druid's hands.
숲지기 사슴의 뿔로 엮은 부적. 사냥꾼은 이걸 쏘지 않은 사슴에게서 받았: A talisman woven from the antlers of the forest's warden stag. The hunter says it was a gift from a stag they chose not to shoot.
